title: Runbook — validating a remediation with a SUSE Security repository scan
text: Scope: confirming, from an authority that is not the agent that produced the patch, that a remediation actually removed a vulnerability. Why a second opinion is structural: the agent that wrote the change is the worst possible judge of whether it worked, and a model asked to confirm its own output will tend to confirm it. The validation step therefore calls the SUSE Security controller REST API rather than reasoning about the diff. Procedure. 1. Exchange the injected API key for a session token: POST /v1/auth, which returns an X-Auth-Token to use on subsequent calls. 2. Request a scan of the rebuilt image: POST /v1/scan/repository with the registry, repository and tag. 3. Poll GET /v1/scan/repository/{id} until the scan completes, then read the vulnerability list. 4. Compare against the pre-remediation scan and report the difference: which CVEs cleared, which remain, and which are new. A remediation that clears the target CVE while introducing two others has not succeeded. 5. Post the diff as a comment on the change, so the human reviewer sees evidence rather than an assertion. Note on scope: the validation agent may request scans and read results. It may not create or modify policy rules, admission rules or groups. That boundary is enforced by the sandbox policy before the request is made, not by the API's own authorisation, and demonstrating the denial is part of the profile.
